name: instruction-and-format
turns: Give me a markdown table comparing programming languages. It must have a header row plus EXACTLY 3 data rows - no more, no fewer. Columns: Language, Typing, Typical use. No text before or after the table.

Now write me a Python function. Put it in a single fenced code block tagged as python. It should define `def fizzbuzz(n: int) -> list[str]:` returning the FizzBuzz strings for 1..n, and below the function include a line that prints fizzbuzz(15). The code must run as-is under python3 with no edits and no imports of anything unavailable.
In AT MOST 15 words, explain why binary search is faster than linear search. Do not exceed 15 words.

Explain the time complexity of binary search and state the recurrence, using inline LaTeX mathematics delimited with dollar signs (like $O(\log n)$) rather than plain text notation. Two short paragraphs.
Reponds entierement en francais, sans un seul mot d'anglais: explique en trois phrases ce qu'est une table de hachage et pourquoi ses recherches sont rapides.
